slides.title: Siddhidatri, the giver of fulfilment
slides.sub: The ninth form of Durga, worshipped on Navami

slides.title: The ninth and last form
slides.body: The giver of siddhis, spiritual attainments. She is worshipped by gods, sages and seekers, and her day closes Navratri with prayers for fulfilment.

slides.title: Seated on a lotus
slides.body: She sits on a lotus with four arms holding a discus, conch, mace and lotus. Many households hold a havan and kanya pujan on Navami.

slides.text:
सिद्धगन्धर्वयक्षाद्यैरसुरैरमरैरपि ।
सेव्यमाना सदा भूयात् सिद्धिदा सिद्धिदायिनी ॥
slides.translit: Siddha gandharva yakshadyair asurair amarair api, sevyamana sada bhuyat siddhida siddhidayini
slides.meaning: May Siddhidatri, served always by siddhas, gandharvas, yakshas, asuras and gods alike, grant us fulfilment.

slides.title: Navami: homa, bhog and the last night
slides.sub: The final full day of Durga Puja worship

slides.title: The Navami puja
slides.body: The priest worships Durga and every deity of the image with flowers, lamps, incense, fruit, sweets and cooked offerings. Many pujas hold a Navami pushpanjali too, usually less crowded than Ashtami's.

slides.title: Homa: the fire offering
slides.body: In a small square pit or vessel, the priest offers ghee, bel wood and other materials into a consecrated fire with mantras. It completes and seals the puja. In some pujas the ash is worn on the forehead.

slides.title: Symbolic offerings
slides.body: Historically some households and temples offered animal sacrifice, most often at Sandhi Puja and on Navami. Most pujas no longer do; many ritually cut an ash gourd, sugarcane or banana instead.

slides.title: Joining the bhog queue
slides.body: Ask a volunteer when bhog will be served; it usually follows the midday puja. Some pujas serve only residents or coupon holders. Take only what you will eat: bhog is prasad.

slides.line: Navami night: the last arati, the dhak at full force

slides.title: Navami night. Tomorrow she leaves.
slides.ask: Send it to your Navami crew

caption.en:
Maha Navami 2026 in Kolkata: the last full day of Durga Puja 🔥

Navami is Tuesday 20 October. The Navami puja, then the homa, a fire offering of ghee and bel wood that seals the worship of the days before.

The bhog is usually the biggest of the festival: khichuri, labra, fried brinjal, chutney, payesh. Many neighbourhood pujas serve anyone in the queue, others use coupons, so ask a volunteer.

By evening it turns bittersweet. Navami night is the goddess's last night on earth, the arati and dhunuchi naach go on till late, and it is one of the two most crowded nights in the city.

Khichuri or labra, what makes Navami bhog for you? Tell us in the comments 👇

slides.title: Navratri in Kolkata: garba, Golu, Ravan dahan
slides.sub: Your own customs, alongside the city's pujo

slides.title: A city of many Navratris
slides.body: Kolkata spends the nine nights on Durga Puja, but Gujarati, Marwari, Punjabi, Bihari, Odia, Tamil and Telugu families keep their own customs alongside the pandals.

slides.title: Ravan dahan
slides.body: In recent years the city's biggest has been at Central Park, Salt Lake, by the Salt Lake Sanskritik Sansad, with effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad. Check the organisers' announcement for the date.

slides.title: Mostly ticketed nights
slides.body: Run by community associations, clubs, hotels and event companies, plus private family gatherings. They're announced close to Navratri, and most run late, so a pandal visit fits in the early evening.

slides.line: Invited to see a Golu? Go in the evening, accept the sundal

slides.title: Vrat while pandal hopping
slides.body: Most food around the pandals isn't vrat food, and bhog is cooked with rice, lentils and ordinary salt. Eat a vrat meal first, carry fruit, roasted makhana and water, and call pure-veg restaurants ahead.

slides.title: Dussehra and Dashami
slides.body: Most national calendars put Dussehra a day before Bengal's Bijoya Dashami. Follow your own panchang for fasting and home rituals, and the Bengal dates for the pandals.

slides.title: Which custom does your family keep?

caption.en:
Navratri in Kolkata during Durga Puja: garba nights, Golu, Ravan dahan and vrat food 🪔

Kolkata spends the nine nights on Durga Puja, but the city's Gujarati, Marwari, Punjabi, Bihari, Tamil and Telugu families keep their own customs too. In recent years the biggest Ravan dahan has been at Central Park in Salt Lake, garba and dandiya nights are mostly ticketed, and Tamil and Telugu homes keep Golu.

Fasting? Most pandal-side food isn't vrat food, so eat a proper vrat meal before you head out and carry fruit, makhana and water.

slides.title: Labra, the soft mixed veg of bhog
slides.sub: Panch phoron, ginger, no onion or garlic

slides.title: Oil, spices, vegetables
items: 2 bay leaves and 2 dried red chillies
250 g red pumpkin, peeled, 3 cm chunks
1 large potato (200 g), peeled, 3 cm chunks
1 small sweet potato (120 g), peeled, 3 cm
1 small white radish (100 g), peeled, batons

slides.title: Beans, greens and the rest
items: 6 to 8 sheem or green beans, 4 cm pieces
1 tbsp ginger paste, 2 green chillies, slit
1 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp ground cumin
1 cup chopped pui shaak or spinach

slides.title: Cut even, smoke the oil
slides.body: Cut the vegetables to about the same size; keep the aubergine in water. Heat the mustard oil till it just smokes, lower to medium, and crackle the bay leaves, red chillies and panch phoron for 20 to 30 seconds.

slides.title: Hard vegetables first
slides.body: Fry the potato, sweet potato and radish with a pinch of turmeric for 5 minutes. Add the pumpkin, beans and drained aubergine and stir-fry 3 to 4 minutes more.

slides.title: Spices, then simmer
slides.body: Add ginger paste, green chillies, turmeric, cumin and salt with 2 tbsp water; stir 2 minutes. Pour in ½ cup water, cover and cook on low-medium 12 to 15 minutes, until the pumpkin starts to break down.

slides.title: Greens and ghee
slides.body: Add the greens and sugar and cook uncovered 3 to 4 minutes, until wilted and moist but not watery. Stir in the ghee, turn off the heat and rest a few minutes before offering.

slides.title: Save this for the bhog kitchen
slides.ask: Save it with the khichuri recipe

caption.en:
Labra recipe: the soft mixed vegetable beside khichuri in Durga Puja bhog 🎃

Pumpkin, potato, sweet potato, radish, aubergine and greens, cooked with panch phoron, ginger and a little sugar until some pieces just begin to break down. No onion or garlic. About an hour.

The trick is the order. Hard vegetables go in first and soft ones after, so some hold their shape and some melt. Keep it moist, not soupy, and watch the fenugreek in the panch phoron; it turns bitter if it goes dark.
